newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's banks mull joint action to clear debts.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's banks mull joint action to clear debts.

text.p: A handful of private banks in Vietnam are holding talks on establishing a mutual fund to solve a cash-crunch which has sparked talk of a sector-wide debt crisis, a senior banker in Ho Chi Minh City said on Thursday.
"As step one we will try to associate...to strengthen our force," the banker, who declined to be named, told Reuters.

"When I talk about association, that means we can organise a kind of syndicate of banks to lend money. So we may organise a small clearing house among the banks in order to settle the individuals' debts," he said.
He said mergers, injections of fresh capital from shareholders or even from the four big state-owned banks could come later.

Fears for the health of the privately held joint-stock banks, of which there are more than 50, have been fuelled recently by mounting revelations of exposure to the ailing property market in the south of the country.

The problem came under the spotlight in February after reports that a highly respected bank, the Joint-Stock Commercial Bank for Private Enterprises (VP Bank), had failed to meet the payment deadline on a $3 million deferred letter of credit.
The industry was shaken again last month when two prominent business executives were arrested in Ho Chi Minh City for their alleged involvement in a massive bank loans scam.
Bankers and economists put the stock of outstanding short-term debt at $1.2-1.5 billion and estimate that about half of that sum should be classified as unrecoverable.

"With the private banking system still in its infancy, it has proved relatively easy for unscrupulous borrowers to raise money against their property at more than one bank," the state-controlled Vietnam Economic Times said.
One industry source said VP Bank was negotiating to extend the repayment date on a clutch of letters of credit worth $19 million, a sum not far short of its legal capital of about $22.3 million.
A veteran banker, Huynh Buu Son, has been brought in as new director general at VP Bank and central bank approval of his appointment is now pending.
Son, 51, has been involved in banking for 30 years, working most recently at the Saigon Bank for Industry and Trade and prior to that at the central bank.
